 Should the Cavaliers choose to make a drastic move, sources suggest that Evan Mobley could be their best asset.
 By Siddhant Gupta Nov 6, 2026 4 min read Oct 31, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Cleveland Cavaliers forward Evan Mobley (4) reacts in the third quarter against the Milwaukee Bucks at Fiserv Forum. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images
 After coming up short in the ECF this year, the Cleveland Cavaliers made some interesting strides toward improving their roster in the offseason. While their core still comprises Donovan Mitchell , James Harden , and Evan Mobley , the acquisition of Peyton Watson seemed promising. Unfortunately, it is safe to say that the squad has faced some early growing pains.
 After eight games in the 2026-27 season, the Cleveland Cavaliers find themselves placing sixth in the East with a 4-4 record. In all fairness, it is very early in the season, and a record like this should not reflect the team’s true potential. However, their consecutive losses to a shorthanded Thunder squad may raise some alarms.
 On paper, the Cavaliers still look like a team with the potential to contend for a title. Still, when factoring in the depth of competition in the Eastern Conference, one could argue that Cleveland may be forced to seek some upgrades. On that note, Bleacher Report’s Grant Hughes recently shared the top three trade assets for each team. With specific reference to the Cavaliers, Hughes ranked Evan Mobley as the team’s best asset, as he wrote:
 “Something significant will have gone wrong with the current core if Mobley’s name winds up in trade talks, but he’d clearly be the Cavs’ most in-demand commodity in that hypothetical. Given the length of Donovan Mitchell’s new extension, the likely lack of interest in James Harden and Jarrett Allen’s ‘meh’ standing among starting centers, Mobley is the one piece that could replenish the war chest in the event of disaster.”
Although Hughes also mentioned the Cavs’ 2033 first-round pick and Peyton Watson as viable assets, in his opinion, Evan Mobley stands out as their most significant trade chip. But is there any truth to this?
In many ways, yes. While the Cavaliers feature other talented players such as Donovan Mitchell, James Harden, and even Jarrett Allen , for that matter, one could argue that Evan Mobley has the most upside.
 Given the way he’s currently playing, Mitchell is likely Cleveland’s only untouchable asset. At 37, with his track record in the playoffs, Harden is unlikely to garner much trade interest at this stage in his career. Although Allen may still have some value as a starting-caliber center, his $28.0 million contract may dissuade teams from pursuing him in light of his averages of 13.3 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks per game this season.
 All things considered, Evan Mobley, at the ripe age of 25, is undoubtedly the Cavaliers’ best trade asset. But would Cleveland even consider moving him?
 The Cavaliers Would Trade Evan Mobley On One Condition
 As mentioned earlier, trading Evan Mobley, especially at this point in his career, doesn’t seem like a wise decision. Mobley has proven himself as an elite two-way player. Aside from winning the DPOY in 2025 and earning two All-Defensive selections, the 25-year-old also possesses a versatile offensive skill set, earning comparisons to NBA legend Kevin Garnett .
 For all intents and purposes, the forward hasn’t given the Cavaliers any reason to trade him either. With averages of 18.8 points, 8.3 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 0.5 steals, and 1.3 blocks per game on 56.0% shooting from the field and 48.6% shooting from three-point range, he is also one of their most consistent performers.
 So what is the one condition on which the Cavaliers would be willing to trade him?
 The chance to acquire a proven playoff riser.
 As reliable as Mobley has been in the regular season, when it comes to the playoffs, the Cavaliers’ forward has struggled to recreate his impact on both ends of the floor.
 Last season’s playoffs are a prime example of this. In 18 appearances, Mobley averaged 17.0 points, 8.1 rebounds, 3.9 assists, 0.9 steals, and 1.8 blocks per game while shooting 53.5% from the field and 33.8% from three-point range. While the figures seem solid, barring his perimeter shooting, when it came to the ECF matchup against the Knicks, his average +/- of -15.5, along with 3.0 turnovers per game, highlighted certain inconsistencies in his performance.
 In all fairness, this can be categorized as nitpicking. As a player, Evan Mobley remains a phenomenal two-way threat capable of anchoring Cleveland’s defense. However, considering that the Cavaliers’ title window has essentially been reduced to the two years with James Harden as part of the core, a desperation trade, while ill-advised, would not be out of the question.
 Realistically, the only players the Cavaliers have shown any inclination to trade Evan Mobley for have been Giannis Antetokounmpo and Jaylen Brown . Given the standard that has been set, it is highly unlikely that Cleveland will settle for anything less than a superstar.
